# Terminal page-break fit

Six original controls generated by `tools/terminal_page_break_fit_fixture.py`
use the project's own OPC shell. The reference application exported each PDF;
sources were closed without saving. `tools/terminal_page_break_fit_reference.py`
records package/PDF hashes, page counts and the page containing “After”.

Each page has 328 pt of writing height. A 300 pt paragraph or exact-height
table leaves room for the following 12 pt terminal page-break paragraph: the reference application
produces two pages. With 324 pt before it, the break paragraph moves to page
two and its break sends “After” to page three. Borders on that terminal
paragraph also move. A leading break followed by “After” in the same paragraph
instead produces two pages, even with 324 pt before it.

These controls distinguish a real paragraph mark sharing the terminal break's
line from a leading break. They do not support indiscriminate removal of the
existing leading-break behavior. No corpus content or restricted fonts are
included. The compatibility setting splitting a terminal break from its
paragraph mark is unchanged by this correction.
